open_obligations: Check that 'All of those works' covers Michael et al. (2023) as well as the LLM debate papers
Confirm that the authors' consultancy-like comparison does not amount to a claim about Michael et al.'s debate-vs-consultancy result
out.other_title: Limited setting: no strong judge priors, expertise gap only from source-text access
out.rationale: Michael et al. list a narrow, information-only expertise gap on fiction QA as a limitation; the authors characterize that setting as more artificial than their math setting and describe the difference in it as privileged information rather than a capability gap. This agrees with Michael et al.'s stated limitation rather than arguing that it is flawed, so SUPPORTS, limited to the expertise-gap part of that limitation.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: Whether information-asymmetric QuALITY debate is a good proxy for oversight across a capability gap; covers only the target's statement that its expertise gap is privileged access to a source text, not its points about harder questions or judge priors

text: The authors summarize Michael et al.'s finding that debate beats consultancy for human judges and note their own setup resembles consultancy. They then say these works mainly use QuALITY with verified quotes, and contrast this with their less artificial reasoning domain where the gap is capability rather than privileged information.
title: Kirchner et al. call Michael et al.'s QuALITY human debate setting artificial, with an information gap only
